high.title: Nearly 60% of Foreign Inflows into India-Focused Funds Withdrawn Since 2024 Peak
high.summary: Foreign investors have pulled approximately 60% of cumulative inflows from India-focused equity funds since their 2024 peak, with net outflows of **$9 billion in calendar year 2026 alone**. The primary driver appears to be a global reallocation toward AI-linked US equities and, to a lesser extent, European markets — which registered their first weekly inflow in nearly three months. Gold funds saw modest inflows after prior outflows, suggesting some risk-off repositioning.

medium.title: Indian Bank Drops Capital Raising Plan on Lower ECL Hit
medium.summary: Indian Bank has cancelled its planned equity capital raise after revising its Expected Credit Loss (ECL) provisioning estimate downward, meaning the capital buffer requirement is lower than initially feared. The bank reported a 10% YoY rise in net profit in Q1 FY27, alongside healthy growth in gross advances and deposits. From a macro and sector perspective, this signals that the transition to the ECL provisioning framework — a key regulatory shift for Indian banks — is proving less capital-intensive than markets had anticipated. This is a modestly positive signal for the broader Indian banking sector's capital adequacy outlook, with implications for systemic stability and credit growth momentum.

medium.title: SIF AUM Jumps 29% to ₹17,858 Crore in June; Inflows Surge 171% MoM
medium.summary: Specialised Investment Funds (SIFs) saw AUM surge 29% to ₹17,858 crore in June 2026, with inflows rising 171% month-on-month — a sign of growing appetite for sophisticated domestic investment structures. SIP contributions hit a record high, underscoring robust retail participation in Indian markets. This strong domestic flow data is relevant as a potential offset to the FPI outflows highlighted above — rising DII and retail-driven inflows could cushion Nifty/Sensex downside and reduce INR depreciation pressure stemming from foreign capital exits.

medium.title: Could oil prices spike further? Inside the fragile US-Iran stance in the Gulf
medium.summary:
Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East have escalated following attacks on commercial vessels in the Gulf region, with Iran reportedly seeking to expand strategic influence over the Strait of Hormuz — one of the world's most critical oil transit chokepoints. Gulf nations are treading carefully to avoid direct confrontation, but the risk premium on crude oil remains elevated. For India, which imports approximately 85% of its crude oil requirements, sustained high oil prices represent a significant macro headwind. A prolonged oil price spike would widen India's trade deficit and current account deficit (CAD), exerting depreciation pressure on the INR/USD rate. Higher import costs could also feed through into domestic inflation (CPI/WPI), complicating the RBI's monetary easing calculus. Bond investors should monitor crude closely — a deteriorating CAD could trigger FPI outflows from G-Secs and push yields higher. Watch for any escalation near the Strait of Hormuz as the key trigger for the next leg up in oil prices and associated INR weakness.
